tldr: The paper proposes a Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning (HDRL) framework that decomposes multi-year infrastructure maintenance planning into a Budget Planner (allocating annual budgets) and a Maintenance Planner (prioritizing assets), integrating linear programming projection within a hierarchical Soft Actor-Critic approach to handle combinatorial action spaces and budget constraints.
contributions: Proposing a two-level hierarchical DRL framework that structurally separates macro-budget decisions from asset-level prioritization
Integrating linear programming projection within a hierarchical SAC framework to ensure rigorous budget compliance
Demonstrating scalability across sewer networks of varying sizes (10, 15, and 20 sewersheds)
Showing superior convergence, stability, and scalability compared to Deep Q-Learning and enhanced genetic algorithms
methods: The proposed HDRL framework decomposes the problem into two hierarchical levels: a high-level Budget Planner that allocates annual budgets within explicit feasibility bounds, and a low-level Maintenance Planner that prioritizes assets within the allocated budget using a hierarchical Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) approach. A linear programming projection step ensures selected maintenance actions maximize system performance while remaining within allocated budgets. The method addresses the exponential growth of combinatorial action spaces inherent in single-agent RL approaches. Validation was conducted through a sewer network case study with 10, 15, and 20 sewersheds, benchmarked against Deep Q-Learning and enhanced genetic algorithms.
results: The HDRL framework converges more rapidly, scales effectively, and consistently delivers near-optimal solutions even as network size grows, compared to conventional Deep Q-Learning and enhanced genetic algorithms. The methodology was tested on sewer networks with 10, 15, and 20 sewersheds, demonstrating robust convergence, superior stability, and scalability advantages over conventional RL methods.
limitations: The study is limited to a single case study (sewer networks), which may limit generalizability to other infrastructure types

The canonical formulation assumes perfect observations and completely certain deterioration models, though the paper acknowledges that measurement errors or model uncertainties would require a POMDP formulation
Constrained DRL approaches broadly face challenges such as duality gaps and feasibility guarantees, as noted in the literature review
